raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Before this change, out-of-tree (OOT) platform plugins register eager fused-op implementations through
[`BaseFusedOp.register_oot_forward()`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46caa54562a97e71d9b937c62875c90b39274b0d/python/sglang/kernels/fused_op.py#L375).
[`BaseFusedOp._resolve_forward_method()`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/46caa54562a97e71d9b937c62875c90b39274b0d/python/sglang/kernels/fused_op.py#L539)
selects the function for the active platform and binds it to the operator with
`registered.__get__(self)`. This works eagerly without adding a
`forward_<platform_key>` method to the operator class.


Out-of-tree platform plugins can register eager fused-op implementations without defining platform-specific methods on operator classes. However, model compilation currently has no equivalent registration API.

Eager dispatch also binds registered functions directly to the operator instance. When PyTorch saves compiler guards, it can look up a bound method by name. A registered function may have no matching class attribute, causing serialization to fail.

Provide an explicit OOT compile registration API and store plugin functions in a form that supports both eager execution and compiler guard serialization. Plugins can choose their compile implementation independently while keeping normal PyTorch tracing behavior.


## Modifications

- Add `BaseFusedOp.register_oot_compile_forward(op_cls, fn, platform_key)`.
  Selection uses the exact operator type and active OOT platform, before the
  existing subclass compile-selection method.
- Store registered functions without binding them to the instance.
  `_forward_oot()` and `_forward_oot_compile()`, defined on `BaseFusedOp`, call
  them with the operator instance as `self`. The active and saved forward
  methods can therefore be resolved by name during guard serialization.
- Preserve eager dispatch precedence, rebinding of registered Python methods,
  compile fallback behavior, explicit/forced backend priority, trace labels,
  and repeated enter/leave restoration.
- Trace the registered function's body as part of the enclosing model.
  Unsupported tracing operations still fail with `fullgraph=True`; normal
  graph-break behavior applies with `fullgraph=False`.
- Add test cases using a fake OOT platform and tensor operations,
  including the guard-serialization regression. Document the registration API.

A plugin can register the same function for both modes, or use separate
implementations with the same signature and behavior:

```python
BaseFusedOp.register_oot_forward(Op, eager_forward, platform_key)
BaseFusedOp.register_oot_compile_forward(Op, compile_forward, platform_key)
```

## Accuracy Tests

### CPU functional checks — passed

Verified with Python 3.12 and PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130:

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/kernels/test_fused_op_dispatch.py -q
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/kernels/test_fused_op.py -q
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/kernels/test_kernels_namespace.py -q

python -m pytest test/registered/unit/platforms/test_platform_interface.py -q
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner_backend/test_full_cuda_graph_backend.py -q
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_cuda_graph_config_backends.py -q
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/compilation/test_torch_compile_decoration.py -q
```
**293 tests passed, plus 25 platform subtests**.

- 293 tests passed, plus 25 subtests.
- Includes 73 dispatch tests, with 38 new cases covering OOT registration, compilation, restoration, and guard serialization.
- The serialization regression failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- The compiler matrix covers eager/Inductor, both fullgraph settings, caching enabled/disabled, and cold/warmed instances.

### GPU numerical parity and model accuracy

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/activation/test_fused_op_gpu_parity.py -v -ra
```

**13 passed, 17 warnings**


### Additional compiler integration check
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest test/registered/e2e/models/test_transformers_backend_eval.py -v
```

**1 passed, 20 warnings**


## Speed Tests and Profiling

Two-GPU throughput check
```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python -m pytest test/registered/basic_perf/test_torch_compile_throughput.py -v
```
**1 passed, 19 warnings**

## Tests not able to run because of huggingface restriction
```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest test/registered/backends/test_torch_compile.py -v -k mmlu

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest test/registered/moe/test_torch_compile_moe.py -v -k mmlu
```


## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

`registered.__get__(self)`. This works eagerly without adding a
`forward_<platform_key>` method to the operator class.


Out-of-tree platform plugins can register eager fused-op implementations without defining platform-specific methods on operator classes. However, model compilation currently has no equivalent registration API.

Eager dispatch also binds registered functions directly to the operator instance. When PyTorch saves compiler guards, it can look up a bound method by name. A registered function may have no matching class attribute, causing serialization to fail.

Provide an explicit OOT compile registration API and store plugin functions in a form that supports both eager execution and compiler guard serialization. Plugins can choose their compile implementation independently while keeping normal PyTorch tracing behavior.
